@ed@tanous.net does your comment about settable FRU policy https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/74672/comment/a7288ea7_0f713001/ still apply?

Considering that we currently have
```.WriteFru                            method    qyay      -            -```

method on FruDevice and the current patch does not prevent anyone from implementing such a policy in the future 😊

Just to clarify, this implementation is `settable FRU policy`
i.e.,
`
...
.PRODUCT_ASSET_TAG                  property  s         "XXXXXXX" emits-change writable
.PRODUCT_FRU_VERSION_ID             property  s         "1.0" emits-change writable
.PRODUCT_INFO_AM1                   property  s         "XXXXXXXXX" emits-change writable
.PRODUCT_INFO_AM2                   property  s         "Config A" emits-change writable
...
`
Marking as resolved. Let me know if you have further queries 😊

> does your comment about settable FRU policy

The aforementioned review was trying to add a very complex, per entity config file (ie, a platform config essentially).  If we want to have an OVERALL policy on which fields are settable on all FRUs, that seems fine to do.  Overall, I'm in support of this patch/feature.

I also suspect this mode (all fields editable) could just be the default and would save a lot of pain.
Acknowledged.
Set config to all

So before, property was registered if it was not empty OR ```PRODUCT_ASSET_TAG``` and now it is registered only if not empty.

So an empty ```PRODUCT_ASSET_TAG``` would not be settable anymore.

Let's say i set my ```PRODUCT_ASSET_TAG=""``` via DBus, then i cannot update it ever again, right?

I somehow assumed that we are not going to set the property to empty.
I think my assumption is completely wrong.
At the same time, why limit this to only one property. I'm thinking of removing the condition so that same flexibility is provided to other properties.
In the related patch, added dbus function to handle this scenario.
this shows you updated it on D-Bus; can you also provide evidence it made it into the EEPROM?
